KVM_CAP_MAX_VCPU_ID is currently always reporting KVM_MAX_VCPU_ID on all
architectures. However
column3: the amount of usable CPUs is determined

column1: during runtime - it is depending on the features of the machine the code
is running on. Since we are using the vcpu_id as an index into the SCA
structures that are defined by the hardware (see e.g. the sca_add_vcpu()
function)
column2: it is not only the amount of CPUs that is limited by the hard-

column1: ware
column2: but also the range of IDs that we can use.

column1: Thus KVM_CAP_MAX_VCPU_ID must be determined during runtime on s390x
So the handling of KVM_CAP_MAX_VCPU_ID has to be moved from the common
code into the architecture specific code
column2: and on s390x we have to return

column1: the same value here as for KVM_CAP_MAX_VCPUS.
This problem has been discovered with the kvm_create_max_vcpus selftest.
With this change applied
column2: the selftest now passes on s390x
